voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyayas 23–24: on Ramaniyaka Garuda asks his mother why they must obey the serpents; she tells him she was made a slave by her sister's deceit in a wager; he asks the serpents what would free them, and they answer: bring the amrita by force (1.23). He tells his mother he will go and asks what he may eat; she sends him to the Nishadas who live in a remote bay of the ocean, but forbids him ever to kill a brahmin, who would be like fire, and tells him how to know one: the one who sticks in his throat like a swallowed fish-hook, burning like charcoal; she blesses him: may the Wind guard his wings, the Moon his back, Fire his head and the Sun all of him (1.24).
structure: From episode 21 (independent review): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, ≤ 3 s; opening style A: the question over the answer image) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 5 s with the UNVOICED recap band over its first shot (KIT.series.recapBand) → turn at 40–60 % → the cliffhanger image + line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image that dissolves into frame 1 (KIT.series.overlayNextScene). No fire edge in the Garuda arc from here.

strings.recapLine: Garuda carried the serpents to Ramaniyaka.
strings.priceEpithet: the drink of the gods, in heaven
strings.nishadaEpithet: a people of the ocean's bay

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: What price could free a slave?
lines.say: What price could free a slave?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (style A, moving from frame 1): Garuda on Ramaniyaka's beach in the late gold light, wings snapping open from t = 0; the serpents rear round him; high above, the white pot of amrita glows in a vision ring. The question in big text from frame 1; the title in the post.

lines.speaker: garuda
lines.say: Mother, [p:80] why must we obey them?
lines.note: STORY 1 (Garuda speaks) with the unvoiced recap band for its first 2.6 s: a palm grove on the island at evening (NEW LIGHT: amber through palms, long shadows), Garuda kneeling to his mother.

lines.speaker: vinata
lines.text: "My sister cheated me in a wager. I became her slave."
lines.say: My sister cheated me in a wager. [p:200] I became her slave.
lines.note: STORY 2 (Vinata speaks): close on Vinata, her head covered (the slave's sari end); in a small memory roundel above her, the black-streaked tail of the white horse (beats[1] 'cheated').

lines.speaker: garuda
lines.text: He asked the serpents: "What will free us?"
lines.say: He asked the serpents: [p:120] What will free us?
lines.note: STORY 3: Garuda strides out of the grove onto the sand and towers over the rearing serpents (a low angle from behind the serpents).

lines.speaker: nagas
lines.text: "Bring us the amrita, by force. Then you are free."
lines.say: Bring us the amrita, [p:100] by force. [p:300] Then you are free.
lines.note: STORY 4 (the price): after a short rest the serpents answer as one; on 'amrita' (beats[0]) the white pot appears far above in the sky in a ring of light, on 'force' (beats[1]) a drum; name plaque 'Amrita'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The price of his mother's freedom: the drink of the gods.
lines.say: The price of his mother's freedom: [p:120] the drink of the gods.
lines.note: FRAME (Sauti at the Naimisha fire, a tenth angle: from behind the sages' shoulders, the fire between them and Sauti, his hand cupped as if holding a pot).

lines.speaker: garuda
lines.text: "I will bring it. But what may I eat on the way?"
lines.say: I will bring it. [p:150] But what may I eat on the way?
lines.note: STORY 5 (Garuda speaks): on the shore at dusk, Garuda half-spread, ready to fly; Vinata before him.

lines.speaker: vinata
lines.text: "In a bay of the ocean live the Nishadas. Eat them."
lines.say: In a bay of the ocean [p:80] live the Nishadas. [p:150] Eat them.
lines.note: STORY 6 · THE TURN (≈ 52 %): after a 0.85 s rest (the episode's one long rest), Vinata names the food; a cut to the bay at moonrise (NEW LIGHT: teal and silver): a far village of huts on stilts, fishing boats, small fires; name plaque 'The Nishadas'.

lines.speaker: vinata
lines.text: "But never a brahmin. He would burn in your throat like fire."
lines.say: But never a brahmin. [p:250] He would burn in your throat [p:60] like fire.
lines.note: STORY 7 (Vinata speaks): close on Vinata, her hand raised in warning (beats[0]); on 'throat' a glowing coal of fire appears at the throat of a painted Garuda silhouette beside her (the sign she gives him, CE 1.24).

lines.text: She blessed him: may the Wind guard your wings, the Moon your back, Fire your head, and the Sun all of you.
lines.say: She blessed him: [p:100] may the Wind guard your wings, [p:60] the Moon your back, [p:60] Fire your head, [p:60] and the Sun all of you.
lines.note: STORY 8: Garuda rises into a deep night-blue sky over the sea; the four guardians appear around him one by one as painted signs on the beats: the Wind's streamers at his wings, the Moon's crescent at his back, Fire's flame above his head, the Sun's disc behind all of him.

lines.text: He swooped down on the Nishadas, and swallowed something that burned.
lines.say: He swooped down on the Nishadas, [p:120] and swallowed something [p:120] that burned.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (cliffhanger image, the catalog line): Garuda dives on the bay, beak open, the huts and boats sweeping toward him; on 'burned' (beats[2]) a coal-red glow lights inside his throat and he jerks his head up.
